findings.finding: E2E test client/e2e/flows/triage-deferred-envelope.spec.ts seeded item id 'trg-toSnooze1', which fails server-side TRIAGE_ID_RE (/^trg-[0-9a-fA-F]{8}$/) validation in triage-validation.ts, so the Snooze click in that test would receive 400 invalid_triageId and the modal would never close, timing out the assertion.
findings.suggestion: Rename the id to a valid 8-hex-char id, e.g. trg-a0000001.

findings.finding: TriagePage's empty-state banner ('No triage items pending. Checkmark') was gated only on totalTriage===0 (open-item count from /api/triage/counts), but PerProjectTriageSection now renders whenever EITHER open or deferred items exist. A project with 0 open items and 1+ parked items shows a populated Deferred section while the page simultaneously claims nothing is pending — a self-contradicting state for exactly the feature this iterate exists to fix.
findings.suggestion: Extend GET /api/triage/counts to also return deferredTotal (cross-project count of status===snoozed items), and gate the empty-state on totalTriage===0 && totalDeferred===0.

findings.finding: The severity-rank map ({critical:0, high:1, medium:2, low:3, info:4}) is duplicated across triage-contract.ts, PerProjectTriageSection.tsx, and two test files with no shared constant.
findings.suggestion: Centralize into one exported constant on a future touch of this area; not worth blocking this PR, two of the three duplications are unavoidable across the client/server package boundary (DO-NOT rule 7).

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: A due park always shows up as OPEN, never lingers as deferred (the revisit-expiry overlay never serves a stale due-state). — readAllItems() bakes applyDeferOverlay(resolveUnion(rawLines), new Date()) into a 5-second TTL, mtime-keyed cache. The cache-hit check only compares file mtimes + elapsed time, never re-derives `now`. Filling the cache at 23:59:58 UTC and reading again at 00:00:02 UTC the next day (4s later, same TTL window, no file write) returns the SAME cached array computed against yesterday's `now`, so a park due that day still reads status:snoozed for up to ~5s. POST /promote|/dismiss|/snooze all call this same cached read for their pre-check and would incorrectly 409 with triage_item_not_in_triage_state for an item that should already be open. FIXED: CacheEntry now stores the pre-overlay rawItems plus an overlayDay (UTC calendar day) alongside the post-overlay items; a cache hit on the SAME day returns items unchanged (same reference), a hit whose day has turned over re-applies applyDeferOverlay to the cached rawItems (no re-read/re-parse) and updates overlayDay. Verified with two new fake-timer tests in triage-store.test.ts: one proves the day-boundary re-derivation fires and revisitDue flips true; the other proves same-day reads still return the identical array reference (the pre-existing invariant is preserved).

Claim under doubt: The revisit-expiry overlay is applied exactly once per resolved view, never re-applied to its own output. — Traced every call site: applyDeferOverlay is called from exactly two places (readAllItems, readAllItemsWithDeliveredOrigin), both applying it once to fresh resolveUnion(...) output. buildTriageListing never calls the overlay; enrichPendingDelivery/enrichWithCampaignRefs mutate only pendingDelivery/campaignSlug on request-scoped shallow clones, never the shared cached array. Could not construct a double-application or cache-corruption scenario. HELD UP — no change needed.

Claim under doubt: Adding revisitAt to the status-event wire line does not change the accepted risk calculus of the two non-composing lock primitives (proper-lockfile vs the sibling monorepo's Python file lock). — revisitAt rides the exact same status event line as the pre-existing by/reason/promotedTaskId fields, written via the same single JSON.stringify(...) + appendFileSync call already covered by triage-write.ts's documented line-atomicity + residence-mis-derivation-is-non-lossy reasoning. Could not find a revisitAt-specific new corruption/loss mode beyond what the existing accepted-risk note already covers for that line's other fields. HELD UP — no change needed.

Claim under doubt: The Deferred section is genuinely read-only — no path lets an operator mutate a deferred item's state. — TriageDetailModal.tsx gates the entire action row (Fix now/Dismiss/Snooze/Promote) behind item.status === "triage" as a React conditional — no DOM node exists for a snoozed item, so there is no reachable keyboard-nav or stale-testid path. DeferredTriageSection's only interactive element opens the same gated modal. Could not find a mutation path reachable from a deferred item. HELD UP — no change needed.
